misconceptions.description: Narrating the exact same words shown on screen, violating the redundancy principle and splitting the visual channel
misconceptions.trigger: learner pairs a full text paragraph with narration that reads it verbatim
misconceptions.feedback: Do not narrate identical on-screen text word for word. Either narrate over a visual or show the text, not both saying the same thing.

misconceptions.description: Believing narration is always superior to text, ignoring that the modality benefit depends on transient content, learner control, and context
misconceptions.trigger: learner converts a reference table or complex equation to audio-only narration
misconceptions.feedback: The modality principle has limits. Reference, complex, or learner-paced content often belongs as inspectable text, not transient audio.

misconceptions.description: Thinking modality means adding more media channels rather than offloading words from the overloaded visual channel to the audio channel
misconceptions.trigger: learner adds narration on top of dense on-screen text and a busy diagram
misconceptions.feedback: Modality offloads words to audio so the eyes can process the graphic. Stacking text plus audio plus a busy image overloads, not offloads.

misconceptions.description: Choosing audio-only narration without a text equivalent, excluding deaf or hard-of-hearing learners and those without audio
misconceptions.trigger: learner ships narration with no captions or transcript
misconceptions.feedback: A modality choice must include an equivalent. Provide captions or a transcript so the audio channel does not gate access.
